answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making every identity post a locked bond before its votes count. Each new agent must stake its own deposit, so an attacker who fabricates a thousand fake peers must lock a thousand separate bonds, and any proven fraud slashes each one. The price of a Sybil swarm thus rises with its size, while an honest agent pays only one modest bond. Even at the market's nadir, when a false whisper about a rival spreads, the forfeitable stake stays the thread that ties every vote to real capital, so manufacturing identities never undercuts earning trust.
